Research

All research

My work explores quantum matter and many-body dynamics in settings that are accessible to current or near-term quantum simulators, from ultracold atoms to quantum computers.

  • Transport properties

    How charge, spin and heat move through strongly interacting, low-dimensional quantum systems.

    4 papers

  • Open and monitored dynamics

    Out-of-equilibrium states produced by measurement or dissipation, increasingly relevant for quantum computers.

    5 papers

  • Strongly correlated phases

    Ground states and equilibrium phases where quantum fluctuations compete with strong interactions.

    9 papers

  • Numerical methods

    Efficient classical simulation of quantum states with tensor networks, numerical path integrals and machine learning.

    10 papers

About

I am a postdoctoral scholar at the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics. I received my Ph.D. in theoretical physics from Cornell University, where I studied under Erich Mueller. My undergraduate degree is in Physics and Italian from Georgetown University, where I rowed on the lightweight crew team.

Outside of physics, I enjoy cooking, traveling, hiking, rock climbing and playing tennis.
